risk_flags.reason: The migration executes `DROP TABLE documents` then recreates it (files/scripts/migrate-tighten-description-topic.js:22-23, diff.patch:27-28). `documents` is the Parent-of-Sacred table that cascades into `questions` and through it `session_answers`. In SQLite a DROP TABLE on a parent fires foreign-key ON DELETE CASCADE actions, so this is a live data-loss path for two sacred tables — the exact table-swap-on-documents pattern that destroyed 790 questions and 746 answers on 2026-04-27. The recreated table also carries no foreign keys or indexes and hardcodes a column list, silently dropping any other columns/constraints present on the real table.

Verification is inadequate to prove acceptance criterion 2 (no data loss). The script and its evidence only count rows in `documents` (22 -> 22, evidence/migration-output.txt:2-3); it never checks `questions` or `session_answers`. Per sacred-data doctrine, covering only the directly-modified table is not verification when cascades make dependent tables part of the operation — a cascade-delete of all questions/answers would leave the documents count unchanged and pass this check. The migration was already executed against the DB (executor_report commands_run), so any cascade loss has already occurred.
